observations.notes: 9M26 rev $22.48bn, EBITDA $5.52bn, CFO $3.68bn, PAT $4.73bn (vs -$117.2m 9M25); swung to net cash $650.8m (debt cut to $5.67bn at mid-26). IPO of 4.1bn shares at NGN 525 (~$1.63bn) launched to fund 1.4 mbpd expansion.

debt_maturities.source: IPO Prospectus & 9M26 release: $5.67bn total debt at Jun-26 incl. $750m 7.50% Jul-31 notes and DIL loans.

recovery_analysis.thesis: Dangote Refinery swung to $5.52bn EBITDA and $4.73bn net profit on $22.48bn revenue in 9M26, flipping from $1.73bn YE25 net debt to $650.8m net cash. However, 9M26 margins benefited from Middle East disruption, 30-40% of crude is imported, and $15-16bn Lamu/1.4mbpd capex plus $3.99bn DIL parent loans require covenant clarity. Structural recovery anchored by Nigeria energy asset perimeter and DAPERE 7.50% Jul 2031 ($750m 144A, issued Jul-26) seniority.

annotations.note: 9M26 rev $22.48bn, EBITDA $5.52bn, PAT $4.73bn; shifted from $1.73bn net debt (YE25) to $650.8m net cash.
100% of crude/refined product export proceeds flow directly into offshore collection accounts; debt service for international Eurobonds is deducted prior to any fiscal repatriation.
Low cash lifting cost ($8 - $18/boe) ensures robust operating profitability and positive cash flow even during severe oil price downturns ($50/bbl).
Proved plus probable commercial reserves provide a durable 12-18 year production life, underpinning long-dated senior paper.

refinery_commercial_scale_and_yield.naira_crude_sales_agreement: Bespoke agreement with NNPC / Federal Government of Nigeria for 385,000 bpd of domestic crude supply payable in Nigerian Naira (NGN), eliminating foreign exchange rationing risks

macroeconomic_and_fx_import_substitution.annual_fx_savings_for_nigeria: $25.0B+ annual reduction in national import bill by substituting refined petroleum imports with domestic production

verdict.stance: Neutral / Cash Surge vs Feedstock, DIL Governance & Lamu Capex Risk
verdict.summary: Dangote Refinery swung to $5.52bn EBITDA and $4.73bn net profit on $22.48bn revenue in 9M26, flipping from $1.73bn YE25 net debt to $650.8m net cash. However, 9M26 margins benefited from Middle East disruption, 30-40% of crude is imported, and $15-16bn Lamu/1.4mbpd capex plus $3.99bn DIL parent loans require covenant clarity.

positives: Rapid operational ramp: 1H26 PAT ~$1.8bn (helped by regional refining cracks) reduced gross debt to $5.67bn at 30-Jun-26 (from $6.24bn Dec-25).
Capital market validation: Priced inaugural $750m 7.50% 2031 senior notes (Jul-26) and launched Oct-26 IPO equity raise.
Strategic domestic scale (650kbpd nameplate) replacing Nigerian refined product imports.
negatives: Crude feedstock bottleneck: 30-40% imported crude required as Nigerian crude is heavily encumbered by oil-backed pre-export loans.
Related-party & expansion overhang: $3.99bn loans from parent DIL (Dec-25), potential $15-16bn expansion / 1.4mbpd target, and Kenyan/legal headlines.
Nigeria sovereign ceiling (B / B3 / B) exposes naira-vs-dollar mismatch risks; legacy repo financials are unverified.
